recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Further FHIR-39393 edits would be redundant unless a separate future work group decision broadens this issue to other canonical resource version definitions.
issue_request: FHIR-39393 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I clarification for R5 asking that StructureDefinition.version stop implying the version value should be a timestamp. The resolution required the long definition to describe an arbitrary, not-globally-unique business version, encourage StructureDefinition.versionAlgorithm[x] for comparisons, allow ISO date/time syntax only when no managed version exists, and copy that wording plus the business versionId note into structuredefinition.html#metadata.
initial_application: Git commit 0d50282ebfa2b0de1eaf2a141e4e54d2bbd3e2b8, titled 'FHIR-39393 StructureDefinition suggests version is a timestamp', applied the issue by changing source/structuredefinition/structuredefinition-StructureDefinition.xml and source/structuredefinition/structuredefinition-introduction.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists structuredefinition=StructureDefinition in the active [resources] section, confirming the inspected StructureDefinition files are in build scope. FHIR-I WGM minutes record the issue as Persuasive with an 11-0-1 vote and say to use the text in the version element definition. The linked Zulip thread confirms that the original concern was whether profile versions must be timestamps and notes versionAlgorithm support; no conflicting later decision was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active StructureDefinition.version definition already contains the approved arbitrary-version, versionAlgorithm, and optional ISO date/time wording, and the metadata table already includes the same clarification plus the business versionId note.
